Overview Sandbox Welchol is a bile acid sequestrant approved by the FDA for the treatment of primary hyperlipidemia and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Common side effects include constipation, indigestion, nausea, and nasopharyngitis. The recommended dosage is 3.75 grams daily, either as 6 tablets once daily or 3 tablets twice daily. It is used as an adjunct to diet and exercise to lower elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with primary hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Type IIa), either as monotherapy or in combination with a statin (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor). It is also indicated for use in boys and postmenarchal girls aged 10 to 17 years with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia if dietary therapy alone has been insufficient and LDL-C levels remain ≥190 mg/dL, or ≥160 mg/dL with a positive family history of premature cardiovascular disease or the presence of two or more other cardiovascular risk factors. Lipid-altering agents should be used alongside a diet low in saturated fat and cholesterol when non-pharmacological interventions alone are inadequate. In patients with coronary heart disease (CHD) or CHD risk equivalents, such as diabetes mellitus, LDL-C treatment goals are <100 mg/dL, with an optional goal of <70 mg/dL for very high-risk patients. If triglycerides are ≥200 mg/dL, non-HDL cholesterol becomes a secondary target, with a goal set 30 mg/dL higher than the LDL-C target. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Welchol is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Diabetes mellitus is considered a CHD risk equivalent, and intensive lipid control is recommended in addition to glycemic management. Off-Label Use and Dosage (Adult) A non-guideline-supported dosage of 3750 mg/day has been used in combination with ezetimibe and a statin.
